AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What do leaves do for a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Hold the tree in the ground
   B. Take in water from the soil
   C. Make the trunk
   D. Use sunlight to make food for the plant

2. Which is a way of protecting ripe fruit from birds and monkeys? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them ripe for months
   B. Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   C. Cut the tree
   D. Poison the animals

3. How far should mulch be from the stem? (1 mark)
   A. A small gap away
   B. Not needed
   C. Piled tightly against it
   D. Ten metres

4. Why is mulch put around a young tree? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   B. It stops flowering
   C. It kills roots
   D. It makes the tree shorter

5. Why should hands be washed after handling chickens? (1 mark)
   A. To remove germs
   B. To get feathers off
   C. To warm the hands
   D. To colour the hands

6. Which of these completes the farm cycle: animals, manure, ____? (1 mark)
   A. Crops
   B. Machines
   C. Bricks
   D. Roads

7. What is the young one of a cow called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Lamb
   C. Kid
   D. Chick

8. What is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. An animal kept and cared for by people
   B. An animal that cannot be tamed
   C. An animal that lives freely in the forest
   D. An animal found only in parks

9. What do protective foods do? (1 mark)
   A. Store water
   B. Build walls
   C. Help the body to fight sickness
   D. Give all the body's energy

10. Which of these is an energy-giving fat? (1 mark)
   A. Spinach
   B. Cooking oil
   C. Oranges
   D. Beans

11. Which drink is best with meals? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty water
   B. Only soda
   C. Only sugary juice
   D. Clean water

12. Which fruit is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Ugali
   C. Chapati
   D. Mango

13. Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan? (1 mark)
   A. A bucket
   B. A spatula
   C. A ladle only
   D. A sieve

14. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   B. To make them raw again
   C. To colour them
   D. To make them larger

15. What is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking in a little oil
   B. Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   C. Cooking in the sun
   D. Cooking without heat

16. What should you do before you start cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Wash your hands
   B. Play with the fire
   C. Take off your shoes
   D. Eat first

17. Why should you wear clean clothes? (1 mark)
   A. To make the clothes wear out
   B. Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   C. To save water
   D. To get tired

18. Why should you not dip hands into a drinking water container? (1 mark)
   A. The container would break
   B. Hands may put germs into the water
   C. Hands would get cold
   D. The water would evaporate

19. What are germs? (1 mark)
   A. Types of food
   B. Large animals
   C. Tiny living things that can cause disease
   D. Kinds of soap

20. Which PPE protects the nose and mouth from dust? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Dust mask
   C. Overall
   D. Gumboots

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

22. Give two disadvantages of shallow frying. (2 marks)

23. Describe how to keep a food journal for one week. (4 marks)

24. Give two reasons why goats are suitable for dry areas. (2 marks)

25. Explain what is wrong with a meal of ugali and salt only, and how to improve it. (3 marks)

26. Give three reasons why fruits are important. (3 marks)

27. Name the three main food groups and one example of each. (3 marks)

28. Why should vegetables not be boiled for a long time? (3 marks)

29. Give three ways of caring for a fruit crop. (3 marks)

30. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)

31. Give two advantages of boiling food. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   Leaves make food using sunlight.

2. B — Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   Peaceful protection.

3. A — A small gap away
   Mulch touching the stem can cause rot.

4. A — It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   Mulch reduces evaporation.

5. A — To remove germs
   Poultry can carry germs.

6. A — Crops
   Manure feeds crops, and crops feed animals.

7. A — Calf
   A calf is a young cow or bull.

8. A — An animal kept and cared for by people
   Domestic animals depend on people for food, water and shelter.

9. C — Help the body to fight sickness
   Vitamins and minerals help protect health.

10. B — Cooking oil
   Oils give a lot of energy.

11. D — Clean water
   Water is essential and healthy.

12. D — Mango
   Mango has vitamins.

13. B — A spatula
   A spatula lifts and turns food.

14. A — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

15. B — Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   Boiling uses hot water.

16. A — Wash your hands
   Clean hands prevent germs.

17. B — Dirty clothes can carry germs and smell
   Clean clothes keep us fresh.

18. B — Hands may put germs into the water
   Use a clean cup or tap.

19. C — Tiny living things that can cause disease
   Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

20. B — Dust mask
   A dust mask covers the nose and mouth.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It can splash and burn, and too much oil is not good for health.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each disadvantage.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table; write what you eat at every meal; write the group of each food; at the end of the week check which groups were missing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: They eat leaves, shrubs and grass, and can live where cattle find little to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: It only gives energy. Add beans or fish for body-building and vegetables or fruit for protective foods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for problem, 1 for protein addition, 1 for protective addition.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins, they give fibre and water, and they can be sold for money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Energy-giving: ugali; body-building: beans; protective: sukuma wiki (or other correct examples).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group with example.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Long boiling removes vitamins into the water, so they lose their goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watering, weeding, mulching, adding compost, pruning, protecting from animals (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

30. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: It needs no oil and it makes hard food soft and safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.
